Answer: B
Reason: The CT images (Figures 1a-c) demonstrate diffuse, randomly distributed micronodules throughout the lung parenchyma, which is the characteristic radiographic appearance of miliary tuberculosis. This finding aligns with the clinical presentation of prolonged fever and elevated sedimentation rate, whereas the other options describe patterns (large nodules, peribronchovascular distribution, centrilobular nodules, or single mass) that do not match the imaging.
